entities.name: The Luminaries
entities.subtitle: A hidden tradition concerned with balance rather than rule.
entities.summary: An ancient lineage that treats power as disciplined relation between consciousness, emotion, environment and matter.
body: Luminaries do not define themselves through spectacle. Their central discipline is restraint: observe first, understand the field, and intervene only when the action preserves agency rather than replacing it.
Their hidden settlements, outposts and cultural practices exist to sustain knowledge that can become dangerous when stripped of responsibility.

meaning.realization: Greater capability increases responsibility rather than entitlement.

entities.name: The Silent Proving
entities.subtitle: Worthiness observed in an ordinary life.
entities.summary: A Luminary child grows up without knowledge of their lineage. Character is observed through genuine choices, not manufactured tests.
body: The Proving is deliberately invisible to the child. School, friendships, mistakes and difficulties must remain real because a staged test would only measure performance.
Only after readiness is established does the hidden lineage become known.

process.title: Birth into a Luminary family
process.summary: The family carries knowledge the child is not allowed to inherit automatically.

process.title: Ordinary life
process.summary: The family lives among ordinary humans and the child grows without privilege.

process.title: Silent observation
process.summary: Natural decisions reveal intent, values and maturity.

process.title: Return — or permanent exile
process.summary: Lineage is revealed only when the person is genuinely ready.

meaning.realization: Being born near power does not make someone worthy of it.

entities.name: The Cessation
entities.subtitle: The day engineered electrical civilization stopped.
entities.summary: A celestial disturbance disrupts engineered electrical conduction globally while biological electrochemistry continues. Dark Beings amplify the collapse.
body: The Cessation is not meant to function as a convenient story reset. It is a systems failure whose consequences spread through water, food, hospitals, communication, transport and public trust.
The hidden world does not become obvious. Instead, physical collapse and weakened boundaries make reality more ambiguous precisely when people have the least capacity to interpret it.

timeline.title: Engineered conduction fails
timeline.summary: Grids, electronics, batteries and communications become unusable.

timeline.title: Dark Being amplification
timeline.summary: Fear and disorder deepen the failure's human consequences.

timeline.title: Local adaptation
timeline.summary: Communities reorganize around water, food, trust and practical knowledge.

meaning.realization: When scaffolding disappears, character and local capability become visible.

entities.name: Dark Beings
entities.subtitle: Corruption as unresolved intent rather than a separate species.
entities.summary: Humans transformed by accumulated grief, rage, obsession or despair; they grow through negative feedback loops and cannot be meaningfully resolved by simple destruction.
body: A Dark Being amplifies what is already present in people and places. Fear becomes easier to sustain, despair becomes environmental, and conflict feeds the next conflict.
The Luminary answer is restoration where possible: weaken the feeding loop, bind safely, and attempt to recover the human underneath.

meaning.realization: Destroying a carrier does not necessarily resolve the cause.

entities.name: Sunset Moonland
entities.subtitle: A place where exhausted travelers can begin to belong again.
entities.summary: A post-Cessation community built beside water, shaped across several eras by exile, rediscovery and the arrival of people looking for somewhere that can still hold them.
body: Sunset Moonland is not meant to work because it has no problems. Its importance comes from a social fabric where the personal still reaches the system.
For Lucas and Teo, it becomes less a destination than an answer to two different forms of exhaustion.

timeline.title: The exiled Luminary child
timeline.summary: An unworthy child withdraws to the land, stabilizes over decades, and is eventually welcomed back.

timeline.title: The fisherman
timeline.summary: A storm leads a fisherman to the place; he later returns with his wife.

timeline.title: The community grows
timeline.summary: Travelers arrive and an organic settlement develops.

timeline.title: Lucas and Teo arrive
timeline.summary: Their attempt to return home changes when they encounter the settlement.

meaning.realization: A place can become home through the quality of relationships rather than origin.

entities.name: Lucas Menezes
entities.subtitle: He feels the need before he feels his own exhaustion.
entities.summary: A 22-year-old environmental engineering student from Salvador whose instinct to help becomes both his magnetism and his burden.
body: Lucas is defeated by scale rather than cruelty. The more he helps, the more clearly he sees the remaining need.
His arc is not about learning to care less. It is about learning that feeling another person's pain does not create an obligation to personally solve everything.

meaning.realization: Feeling deeply does not require carrying everything.

entities.name: Mateus “Teo” Duarte
entities.subtitle: He reads people quickly enough to find a path through them.
entities.summary: A 21-year-old marine biology student from Florianópolis with an exceptional ability to understand people and turn perception into navigation.
body: Teo can find an angle through almost any individual interaction, but a bureaucracy has no emotional state for him to read.
Where Lucas absorbs pain, Teo converts patterns into movement. Their friendship works because each corrects the other's blind spot.

meaning.realization: Reading people becomes most powerful where the system is built from relationships.

relationships.label: selection practice
relationships.description: The Proving protects Luminary capability from becoming inherited entitlement.

relationships.label: philosophical conflict
relationships.description: Restraint and restoration confront amplification and unresolved intent.

relationships.label: amplified by
relationships.description: Dark Beings deepen the human consequences of a celestial trigger.

relationships.label: reshaped by
relationships.description: The post-Cessation world accelerates the settlement's growth.

relationships.label: closest friend
relationships.description: Lucas sees the pain; Teo sees a way through.

relationships.label: finds belonging
relationships.description: The place challenges his belief that helping means fixing.

relationships.label: finds fit
relationships.description: A community built through relationships matches the way he naturally navigates.
